scenes.title: Room inside the promise
scenes.viewerPurpose: Feel love meeting a person who will change Meet two lovers in a strange but understandable place
scenes.composition: Mara and Sio stand together in a dusk city
addOrChange: Replace rescue boat action with a terrace and clear day-night horizon.

cues.narration: Can you promise to love someone without claiming the person they may become?
cues.visualAction: Offer a hand without pulling the other lover closer.

cues.narration: The Tao of OMIS begins with two lovers in a city between permanent day and night.
cues.visualAction: Reveal the city’s habitable dusk around the pair.

scenes.title: Two finite lovers
scenes.viewerPurpose: Recognize desire memory and staying close Look ahead to worlds with greater powers
scenes.composition: The lovers compare imperfect memories over tea
addOrChange: Briefly open views onto two later worlds without showing plot revelations.

cues.narration: Mara and Sio face desire, imperfect memory, and the work of remaining close.
cues.visualAction: Compare differing recollections while the pair remain together.

cues.narration: Their story leads into two more worlds, where people can do increasingly extraordinary things.
cues.visualAction: Widen to two inhabited worlds while retaining the lovers as reference.

scenes.title: A larger power
scenes.viewerPurpose: Notice understanding someone does not make a relationship equal Picture a knot loose enough to move
scenes.composition: An observer and a finite person share a table with a bowl and loose knot
addOrChange: Remove replica displays and keep the knot an ordinary source-grounded object.

cues.narration: The ability to understand another person grows, but equality does not automatically follow.
cues.visualAction: The observer turns from studying the bowl toward its owner.

cues.narration: A loose knot becomes a small reminder that staying close need not mean holding someone still.
cues.visualAction: Loosen the knot slightly while it continues to hold both ends.

scenes.title: Begin in the dusk
scenes.viewerPurpose: Carry a familiar question about love into unfamiliar worlds Want to begin with the lovers whose promises remain uncertain
scenes.composition: The triptych opens toward its original finite lovers
addOrChange: Remove later children and universe-specific revelation objects.

cues.narration: This science-fiction journey carries a familiar question about love into very unfamiliar worlds.
cues.visualAction: Carry the same love question across the three reading windows.

cues.narration: Begin with the finite lovers, whose uncertain promises give the larger wonders something real to risk.
cues.visualAction: Return to Mara and Sio without fixing their future relationship.
